# ADR-051a — Amendment to ADR-051: the Phase 6 post-deployment observation milestone is waived by owner; ADR-024 reaffirmed (no snapshot for Phase 7)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Amendment to ADR-051 (2026-09-01, Checkpoint 7.8A, owner-approved): the `2026-09-04T20:08:25Z` Phase 6 post-deployment observation milestone is `waived_by_owner`, and ADR-024 is reaffirmed unchanged — no production snapshot is taken for the Phase 7 deployment.** **Milestone waiver.** ADR-052 gated Phase 7's production deployment on that instant "so that a genuine Phase 6 production incident can never be confounded with a Phase 7 change." The owner waives the waiting period on the ground that the purpose is already discharged rather than skipped: a Phase 6 incident occurred, and it is fully isolated — grant loss verified directly in the owner's Google Account linked-apps view, root cause established as non-additive OAuth consent, the mechanism reproducible and traced to one parameter, remediation landed and mutation-proven, no health or calendar data lost, and the backfill behaviour that recovers the gap already verified. There is no residual ambiguity for a Phase 7 rollout to muddy. Recorded status: **`waived_by_owner`**, following the precedent set when ADR-051's own pre-deployment wait was waived in Checkpoint 6.7A. **The waiver removes the waiting period and NOTHING else.** Every technical gate stands: the OAuth consent repair must be complete and verified before deployment, migrations still run from the newly built api image with `--no-deps`, rollback images are still tagged by resolved digest first, and the deployment order frozen in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is unchanged. **Snapshot: NO.** ADR-024 stays Locked and unamended — Personal OS retains no backup system. The exception is refused on the merits rather than by default: migrations `0014` and `0015` are `CREATE TABLE`-only, alter no existing table, and are therefore forward-compatible with the currently-serving images, so rollback is image-only and a dump would protect against nothing a rollback does not already cover. Checkpoint 6.7B's one-off snapshot was an explicitly-approved exception for a deployment whose risk profile differed, and it was deleted at closure precisely to restore this rule (Checkpoint 7.8A, user-approved 2026-09-01)
